parsed.explanation: No statute criminalises trans identity or same-sex conduct, and official posture is cooperative, but the operative risk is documented police behaviour: a national rights body recorded 135+ harassment/abuse cases against trans women on city streets, a city-level police practice of abusing and expelling trans sex workers (forcing naked bathing in filthy water, treatment not applied to cisgender workers), and a survey finding ~38% of trans women arrested, mostly for being trans. That is state-tolerated, trans-specific enforcement at street level — tier 2–3 exposure with no documented remedy. Custody placement is undocumented outside one unenacted surgical-transfer remark. Official non-discrimination findings and a visible scene mitigate somewhat. Visitor-facing severity is harassment, extortion and arrest rather than imprisonment campaigns, but the pattern is recurring and state-linked.

entry_documents.exposure: No gender-marker change possible domestically, but visitors carry home-issued documents; no documented border friction or document-driven denial of entry.
entry_documents.interaction: No documented interaction between document checks and police targeting.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: 38% of surveyed trans women reported arrest, >90% saying it was because they were trans; arrests used as a police lever against trans women in at least one city; prison placement for non-surgical trans prisoners undocumented; overcrowding from crackdowns raises custody risk.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Surgical post-surgery transfer to a women's facility reported by a rights official, but no statute or policy text; unverified.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Custody conditions and placement at other facilities unverified.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No documented facility bans; no official discrimination found in health care or education per the 2017 foreign report.

care_services.exposure: Gender-affirming surgery not legally available; no documented care denial reaching visitors; no documented medication seizure.
care_services.protection: 2017 report found no official discrimination in health care.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Documented police targeting of trans women: forced filthy bathing, expulsion from areas, extortion/abuse; violence against LGBTI persons listed among the country's most significant rights issues; 135+ street harassment/abuse cases.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Information-ministry 2015 letter against media mockery; tourism ministry welcome messaging; UPR acceptance of SOGIESC recommendations (unenacted).
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Police practices are city-level; no breakdown of street harassment across cities.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented for visitors; family rejection and school bullying are resident-facing.
minors_guardians.protection: 2018 nationwide curriculum covering gender identity and anti-discrimination (resident-facing climate signal).

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Frequent harassment and appearance-based bullying documented; 100+ violence/abuse incidents reported by a local LGBTI organisation; police are perpetrators in documented cases, so reporting to police may worsen exposure.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Not documented; no hate-crime statute identified.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Civic-space restrictions (speech/assembly/press) constrain advocacy and recourse.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No statutory anti-discrimination protection on SOGI grounds; no functioning remedy documented against police abuse; claims of existing protection disputed.
remedies_unknowns.protection: National human-rights bodies document abuses (monitoring, not enforcement); UN expert visit produced recommendations.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: UPR acceptances not enacted; monitoring counts are not prevalence rates; survey sampling frame unstated.

anchor_checks.comparison: Less severe than 0.35-A's universal border exclusion register: entry is not systematically denied and there is no visitor-registration or exclusion machinery. Police street abuse is localised rather than universal, but is documented state behaviour, placing this above the 0.35 tier on some axes while lacking its universal exposure.

Comparable to 0.55-B in that harm is administrative/street-level (harassment, humiliation, arrest risk) rather than custodial campaigns, and no execution pathway exists. Police extortion and forced bathing exceed 0.55-B's screening friction in severity, but 0.55-B's border exposure is more universal; net effect keeps this jurisdiction around the same band.

Below 0.75-C: there 0.75-C has trained border officers, working tribunal remedies, and compensation for unlawful detention. Here documented police abuse of trans women recurs, no statutory anti-discrimination recourse exists, and no enforcement mechanism is shown to work, holding the rating well under 0.75.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime pairs a non-criminalising statute book and cooperative official posture with a documented, recurring street-level police practice targeting trans women (abuse, extortion, forced expulsion) and a high reported arrest rate. Severity if outed is harassment, extortion, and possible arrest — not organised sweeps, imprisonment campaigns, or lethal state action — but the state is a direct participant and no working remedy is documented. Protective signals (Pride scenes, tourism welcome, no official discrimination findings) are real but do not constrain police behaviour. A visitor, especially a trans woman visible in public, carries documented exposure to state-linked abuse with thin recourse, situating the jurisdiction in the Elevated Risk band around 0.45.
